core: Who counts as unemployed under the BLS definition: no job, available for work, and actively searched in the prior 4 weeks
The three labor-force categories: employed, unemployed, and not in the labor force (age 16+, civilian noninstitutional)
Unemployment rate = unemployed / labor force x 100, where labor force = employed + unemployed
Labor-force participation rate = labor force / adult civilian noninstitutional population x 100
Types of unemployment: frictional, structural, cyclical, and seasonal (with seasonal adjustment)
Natural rate of unemployment (frictional + structural, cyclical = 0) and full employment
BLS measurement: the Current Population Survey (household survey, ~60,000 households, run by the Census Bureau); the official U-3 rate; discouraged and marginally attached workers; the broader U-6
supporting: One verified worked rate calculation (hypothetical Rivertown) plus the reason a falling rate can be misleading
The current dated headline figure: U-3 = 4.1% in July 2026 (BLS)
outOfScope: Recessions and the mechanics of the business cycle (own topic: economics:foundations:business-cycle) — cyclical unemployment is connected, not re-taught

Wage determination and labor supply/demand (own topic: economics:foundations:labor-markets)

claims.claim: The BLS classifies the civilian noninstitutional population aged 16 and older into employed, unemployed, and not in the labor force.
To be counted as unemployed, a person must have no job, be currently available for work, and have actively looked for work at some time during the prior four weeks.
The labor force is the sum of the employed and the unemployed, and the unemployment rate equals the unemployed divided by the labor force, times 100.
The labor-force participation rate is the labor force divided by the adult (civilian noninstitutional) population, times 100; in the United States it was roughly 61 to 62 percent in recent years.
Frictional unemployment is short-term unemployment from workers moving between jobs or entering the labor market; it persists even in a healthy economy.
Structural unemployment is a lasting mismatch between the skills or locations of workers and the jobs available, often driven by shifts in technology or demand.
Cyclical unemployment is the variation in unemployment caused by the economy moving between expansion and recession (the business cycle).

The natural rate of unemployment is the unemployment remaining when cyclical unemployment is zero (the frictional plus structural components); the economy is at full employment when the actual rate equals the natural rate, with real GDP at potential.
The BLS estimates unemployment from the Current Population Survey, a monthly household survey of about 60,000 households conducted by the Census Bureau.

Marginally attached workers want and are available for work and looked within the past 12 months but not the past 4 weeks; discouraged workers are the subset who did not look because they believed no jobs were available. Neither is counted in U-3.

U-6, the broadest BLS labor-underutilization measure, adds all marginally attached workers and all people employed part time for economic reasons to the unemployed, as a percent of the civilian labor force plus marginally attached workers, and runs well above the official U-3 rate.
The official U-3 unemployment rate in the United States was 4.1 percent in July 2026.

Worked example arithmetic (Rivertown): with 120,000 employed, 8,000 unemployed, and 72,000 not in the labor force out of a 200,000 adult population, the labor force is 128,000, the unemployment rate is 6.25 percent, and the participation rate is 64 percent; verified by computation.

conflictingEvidence.issue: One web-search summary appeared to give marginally attached and discouraged workers identical definitions.
positions: A summary rendered both as 'not in the labor force, want and available for work, looked in the prior 12 months but not the prior 4 weeks.'

The BLS Concepts and Definitions distinguish them: marginally attached workers gave any reason for not searching recently, while discouraged workers are the subset who cited specifically that they believed no jobs were available.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson uses the BLS distinction: discouraged workers are a subset of the marginally attached who did not search because they believed no jobs were available.

conflictingEvidence.issue: The precise July 2026 U-6 value was not cleanly confirmable across sources (estimates near 7.8-7.9%).
positions: Search summaries suggested U-6 near 7.8-7.9% in mid-2026.
No single authoritative dated value could be verified directly because BLS blocked automated fetches.
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson does not assert a precise U-6 figure. It states qualitatively that U-6 runs well above U-3 (often close to double), which is well established, and anchors only the confirmed U-3 = 4.1% July 2026 figure.
